properties.description: Platinum and Ruthenium (2:1) supported on MoC

nodes.name: MoC precursor pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The preparation method of MoC was modified based on previously reported procedures (Supporting Information). For MoC, the change of pyrolysis temperature can induce different structures, which can produce large effect in the support properties. The effect of pyrolysis temperature on the crystallization evolution of MoC has been discussed (700, 800 and 900°C). As evidenced by XRD analysis in Figure S1, only single MoC (PDF#89-2868) phase exists under lower temperature of 700°C and 800°C (labelled as MoC-700 and MoC-800, respectively), and obvious phase transformations to Mo₂C (PDF#35-0787) with main MoC coexistence at 900°C (named MoC-900).

nodes.name: PGM impregnation-pyrolysis on MoC
nodes.procedure: The PGM/MoC were synthesized by simple impregnation-pyrolysis method at 500°C in 5% H₂/Ar atmosphere (Supporting Information), and the amount of PGM has been confirmed by ICP-MS (Table S1). In the following structural characterization, the PtRu alloy catalyst synthesized with a Pt/Ru ratio of 1:2 is taken as a representative sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: MoC-700 shows single MoC phase (PDF#89-2868). All PGM/MoC samples maintain diffraction patterns similar to MoC support with no obvious metallic phase peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As evidenced by XRD analysis in Figure S1, only single MoC (PDF#89-2868) phase exists under lower temperature of 700°C ... The XRD analysis reveals that all PGM/MoC samples maintain diffraction patterns similar to the MoC support, with no obvious diffraction peaks corresponding to metallic phases (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: MoC-700 exhibits Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 558.2 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms (Figure S2), all the three catalysts show porous structures, and MoC-700 exhibits the largest Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area (558.2 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: MoC-700 reveals porous and loose surface morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of MoC-700 reveal a porous and loose surface morphology, facilitating mass transfer and ink dispersion in fuel cells (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: MoC nanoparticles have average size of 2.2 ± 0.5 nm, uniformly dispersed on amorphous carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, TEM images reveal that the MoC nanoparticles with an average size of 2.2 ± 0.5 nm, uniformly disperse on the homologous amorphous carbon (Figure 1a and Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: MoC shows lattice spacings of 0.216 nm and 0.249 nm ascribed to (200) and (111) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacings of 0.216 and 0.249 nm can be ascribed to the (200) and (111) planes of MoC in Figure 1a, consistent with the main facet from XRD pattern in Figure 1b.

nodes.characterization_summary: MoC-700 shows I_D/I_G ratio of 0.83, indicating lower degree of defects than Vulcan XC-72 (1.36).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of MoC-700 shows lower I_D/I_G ratio (0.83) than that of commercial Vulcan XC-72 carbon black (1.36), indicating lower degree of defects and more ordered structure (Figure S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: PGM nanoclusters (<2 nm) are loaded onto MoC support for Pt/MoC, Ru/MoC, and Pt₁Ru₂/MoC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Spherical aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) were conducted to confirm the loading condition of the PGM nanoclusters on the MoC. As shown in Figure 1c-e, the PGM species (Pt, Ru, and PtRu alloy) are loaded onto MoC with smaller nanoclusters (< 2 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt₁Ru₂/MoC shows co-distribution of Pt-Ru within Mo signal, confirming PtRu nanoclusters loaded on MoC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For EDS line scanning on Pt₁Ru₂/MoC, the line profiles revealed the co-distribution and distinct compositional gradients: along the arrow direction ... the complete coverage of Pt-Ru signal within the wider Mo signal well confirmed the loading of PtRu nanoclusters on MoC rather than carbon support.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/MoC shows Pt 4f₇/₂ at 72.0 eV (positive shift vs Pt/C 71.9 eV); Ru/MoC shows Ru 3p₃/₂ at 461.4 eV (positive shift vs Ru/C 461.2 eV); Pt₁Ru₂/MoC shows Pt 4f₇/₂ at 72.1 eV and Ru 3p₃/₂ at 461.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When MoC is employed as the support, Pt/MoC (72.0 eV) exhibits a minor positive shift compared to Pt/C (71.9 eV) ... the binding energy of Ru in Ru/MoC (461.4 eV) displays the +0.2 eV shift relative to Ru/C (461.2 eV) ... the distinct shifts observed for Pt (72.1 eV) and Ru (461.6 eV) in Pt₁Ru₂/MoC.
